title: Compat API: attach to an exited container resets its state and destroys the recorded exit code
body:
### Issue Description

Attaching to an **already-exited** container through the Docker-compatible HTTP API resets that container's state and destroys its recorded exit code. The container reverts from `exited` to `created`, `State.ExitCode` is reset to `0`, and a subsequent `POST /containers/{id}/wait` returns `{"StatusCode":-1}`.

The real exit code is not recoverable afterwards — the engine no longer holds it.

This is a read operation from the caller's point of view, so the data loss is silent and unexpected: the response itself is a normal `200` with the expected log frames, and nothing signals that anything was destroyed.

Notably, `podman attach` on the CLI refuses this case (`can only attach to created or running containers`, cf. #9597, #23757), but the compat API endpoint does not.

`GET /containers/{id}/logs` on the same container does **not** have this effect, and Docker does not have it at all.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

```bash
SOCK=/run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock
N=attach-exitcode-probe

curl -s -o /dev/null -XPOST --unix-socket $SOCK -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"Image":"alpine","Cmd":["sh","-c","exit 4"]}' \
  "http://d/v1.41/containers/create?name=$N"
curl -s -o /dev/null -XPOST --unix-socket $SOCK "http://d/v1.41/containers/$N/start"
curl -s -o /dev/null -XPOST --unix-socket $SOCK "http://d/v1.41/containers/$N/wait"

echo -n 'before: '; curl -s --unix-socket $SOCK "http://d/v1.41/containers/$N/json" \
  | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin)["State"]; print(d["Status"], d["ExitCode"])'
echo -n 'wait:   '; curl -s -XPOST --unix-socket $SOCK "http://d/v1.41/containers/$N/wait"

# the attach that does it -- stream=0, so it returns immediately
curl -s -o /dev/null -XPOST --unix-socket $SOCK \
  "http://d/v1.41/containers/$N/attach?stream=0&logs=1&stdout=1&stderr=1"

echo -n 'after:  '; curl -s --unix-socket $SOCK "http://d/v1.41/containers/$N/json" \
  | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin)["State"]; print(d["Status"], d["ExitCode"])'
echo -n 'wait:   '; curl -s -XPOST --unix-socket $SOCK "http://d/v1.41/containers/$N/wait"
```

### Describe the results you received

```
before: exited 4
wait:   {"StatusCode":4,"Error":null}
after:  created 0
wait:   {"StatusCode":-1,"Error":null}
```

All three attach variants trigger it — `stream=1&logs=1`, `stream=1` alone, and the `stream=0&logs=1` shown above, which returns cleanly in a couple of milliseconds. It is the call itself, not the hang that `stream=1` produces against an exited container.

### Describe the results you expected

Attaching to an exited container should either be refused (as the CLI does) or be a no-op with respect to container state. The recorded exit code should survive, so that:

```
after:  exited 4
wait:   {"StatusCode":4}
```

Docker behaves this way — same probe against Docker 29.7.2 (API 1.55) leaves `exited 4` and `wait` `{"StatusCode":4}` untouched.

### podman info output

```yaml
version:
  APIVersion: 5.8.4
  Version: 5.8.4
  OsArch: linux/amd64
host:
  os: linux
  kernel: 6.12.94+deb13-amd64
  distribution: Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)
  rootless: true
  conmon: 2.1.12
  ociRuntime: crun
```

Reproduced identically on **5.8.4** and on **5.4.2** (the version Debian 13 ships), rootless in both cases.

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

Found while building a pure-Perl Docker Engine API client that is tested against both Podman and Docker. The client now has to ask `inspect` whether the container is running and refuse the attach itself, which costs a round trip and still leaves a race — the container can stop between the check and the attach, and the exit code is then lost the same way. There is no attach-if-running option in the API, so this cannot be fully solved on the client side.

comments.body: I've submitted a PR that fixes the logs-only attach issue for exited containers and adds a regression test. Happy to make any changes if needed : ) https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/29673
